definition: Handling Imbalanced Data is a core concept in Data Science. It refers to the techniques, principles and practices that let a practitioner work effectively with this topic in real systems.

theory.heading: What Handling Imbalanced Data is
theory.body: Handling Imbalanced Data describes the methods and patterns used within Data Science to achieve reliable, maintainable results. Understanding it is the foundation for everything built later in this course.
points: Handling Imbalanced Data is a named, repeatable concept.
It has a clear purpose and scope.
It connects to other course topics.

theory.heading: Why Handling Imbalanced Data matters
theory.body: Without Handling Imbalanced Data, systems built with Data Science are harder to debug, extend and operate. Teams that master this topic ship fewer defects and communicate more clearly about design decisions.

theory.heading: How Handling Imbalanced Data works
theory.body: The mechanism behind Handling Imbalanced Data follows a repeatable sequence: understand the requirement, apply the principle, verify the result and refine based on feedback. Each step has checks that keep the work on track.
points: Apply the core principle of Handling Imbalanced Data.

theory.heading: Advantages and limitations of Handling Imbalanced Data
theory.body: Handling Imbalanced Data offers structure, clarity and consistency, but it also adds overhead and may be overkill for trivial tasks. Use it when the benefit in reliability outweighs the added effort.
points: Limitations: added overhead, not always needed.
